text:
Jordan K: Hi folks, first week here. After switching my Mac to Colima, my postgres service in docker-compose immediately exits with "could not create lock file "/var/lib/postgresql/data/postmaster.pid": Permission denied". I was using a host bind mount for PG data. Also my local Redis sometimes rejects connections with ERR NOAUTH even though I set REDIS_PASSWORD in .env and docker-compose.yml. Any quick troubleshooting steps?

Maya R: welcome Jordan! common Colima issue: host mounts can get root:root ownership inside the Colima VM. For Postgres prefer a named volume, but if you need a host mount do `colima ssh` and chown to uid 999.

Maya R: ```bash
# on your laptop
colima ssh
sudo chown -R 999:999 /path/to/host/pgdata
exit
# then restart the db
docker-compose up -d db
```

Theo: Quick checklist: 1) are you using docker desktop path vs colima path (they differ)? 2) is SELinux/AppArmor in play (unlikely on mac)? 3) did an earlier failed init leave files owned by root? If so remove the volume or fix ownership.

Jordan K: I tried chown inside colima and postgres starts, thanks. But when my init SQL runs it errors with "could not open extension control file "pgvector.control"". I added pgvector to schema.sql locally.

Maya R: That usually means the image doesn't have the extension installed. Our dev image installs pgvector in the Dockerfile. If you used plain `postgres:slim` it might not include the package. Use the repo's dev Dockerfile or add steps: `apt-get update && apt-get install -y postgresql-15-pgvector` in the image build.

Theo: Another way: run the init against a DB that has extensions available, or build a small init image that preloads extensions. Also ensure the image and postgres major version match the .sql extension release.

Jordan K: Redis note: I discovered my .env wasn't being loaded because I was running `docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up` and the file references `.env.dev`. Once I exported REDIS_PASSWORD locally the redis-cli -a <pass> ping returned PONG.

Jordan K: Commands I ran to validate:```bash
# check redis inside container
docker-compose exec redis redis-cli -a "$REDIS_PASSWORD" ping
# check env in container
docker-compose exec redis env | grep REDIS
```

Maya R: ops-bot runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup has Colima sections and our standard dev compose snippets. Also if you switch to named volumes: `docker-compose down --volumes` then `docker-compose up -d` to re-init.

ops-bot: linked doc: /runbooks/local-db-setup — see section "Colima and host mounts". Recommended: use named volumes or chown in colima.

Theo: If you want a quick safe reset: `docker-compose down -v && docker volume prune -f` then ensure your compose uses the official dev image and `docker-compose up -d db`. That will recreate a clean volume with correct permissions.

Jordan K: Great — switching to named volume + using the repo dev image fixed both problems. Appreciate the help! Happy to share exact commands I used in a short doc for the runbook if useful.

Maya R: please do, that would help the next new hire. Welcome aboard :tada:
